module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# A binomial coefficient summation

A binomial coefficient summation: $a(n) = S(3, n) / S(1, n)$, where for a positive integer $r$
we define
$$S(r,n) = \sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \left( \binom{n}{k} - \binom{n}{k-1} \right)^r$$
with $\binom{n}{-1} = 0$.

*References:*
- [A003162](https://oeis.org/A003162)
- H. W. Gould, Problem E2384 (proposal), Amer. Math. Monthly, 81 (1974), 170-171
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA3162

/-- A binomial coefficient summation: $a(n) = S(3, n) / S(1, n)$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  let numerator : ℚ := ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n / 2 + 1),
    let diff : ℚ := (n.choose k : ℚ) - (if k = 0 then 0 else (n.choose (k - 1) : ℚ))
    diff ^ 3
  let denominator : ℚ := (n.choose (n / 2) : ℚ)
  numerator / denominator

/-- Auxiliary sequence $b(n) = a(2n-1)$. -/
def b (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  a (2 * n - 1)

macro "eval_a" : tactic =>
  `(tactic| (dsimp [a]
             norm_num [Finset.sum_range_succ, Nat.choose_succ_succ, Nat.choose_zero_succ]))

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by eval_a

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by eval_a

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 1 := by eval_a

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 3 := by eval_a

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 6 := by eval_a

/--
$a(n)$ is an integer for all $n \ge 0$.

Gould proposed this as Monthly Problem E2384. The 1974 reference in the module docstring
is that proposal, not a solution to it.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem a_is_integer (n : ℕ) : (a n).den = 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Let $b(n) = a(2n-1)$. Then the supercongruence $b(n p^k) \equiv b(n p^{k-1}) \pmod{p^{3k}}$
holds for positive integers $n$ and $k$ and all primes $p \ge 5$.
- Zhi-Wei Sun, Nov 16 2019
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n k p : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hk : 0 < k) (hp : p.Prime) (hp_ge : 5 ≤ p) :
    (b (n * p ^ k)).num ≡ (b (n * p ^ (k - 1))).num [ZMOD (p : ℤ) ^ (3 * k)] := by
  sorry

end OeisA3162

findings.description: The attribution in the docstring (line 86), “Zhi-Wei Sun, Nov 16 2019,” does not match the cited OEIS source. A003162 places this conjecture in Peter Bala's March 26, 2023 comment block; the linked A183069 explicitly attributes the same conjecture to Peter Bala on March 20, 2023. This is an attribution/date slip, not a mathematical misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A003162: “From Peter Bala, Mar 26 2023: (Start)” introduces the block ending with the stated supercongruence. A183069: “We conjecture that the sequence satisfies the supercongruences ... for all primes p >= 5 and positive integers n and k. - Peter Bala, Mar 20 2023.” Read via https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A003/A003162.seq and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A183/A183069.seq.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the attribution with “Peter Bala, Mar 26 2023” to match A003162, optionally also citing the March 20, 2023 comment in A183069.

reformulations.difference: Lean divides by the central binomial coefficient n.choose (n / 2), whereas the source describes the denominator as S(1,n).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing m=floor(n/2), the sum defining S(1,n) telescopes to binomial(n,m), with the k=0 branch implementing binomial(n,-1)=0. This coefficient is positive for every natural n, including n=0, so no division-by-zero default is reachable. The equality with the source quotient and denominator positivity were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Gould's problem is stated as S(1,n) dividing S(3,n); Lean requires the reduced rational a(n) to have denominator 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both sums are integers and S(1,n)=binomial(n,floor(n/2)) is nonzero. Consequently their rational quotient has reduced denominator 1 exactly when the denominator divides the numerator. The exact equivalence was proved as Review3162.a_is_integer_iff_divisibility in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Lean applies integer congruence to the reduced numerators of rational-valued b, rather than directly to the integer sequence values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The sequence is integral, so each reduced numerator represents the sequence value itself. Integrality follows independently from Theorem 4.1(i) of arXiv:1602.04347 by setting m=N+1 and the summation endpoint to floor(N/2), with N=0,1 checked directly. In scratch, Review3162.conjecture_forms_iff proves the congruence equivalent to the difference of the rational sequence values being an integer multiple of p^(3k), with integrality supplied as an explicit premise; it does not assume the supercongruence.

sources_consulted: OEIS A003162, complete entry via the official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A003/A003162.seq (canonical entry: https://oeis.org/A003162).

P. J. Miana, H. Ohtsuka and N. Romero, Sums of powers of Catalan triangle numbers, arXiv:1602.04347v1; especially the definition of C_{m,k}, Theorem 4.1(i), and Conjecture 6.1. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1602.04347
review.notes: No mathematical misformalizations found. All definitions and theorem statements were checked. Lean computation matched the official b-file for every n=0..64, and all 24 supercongruence tests with n in {1,2,3,5}, k in {1,2}, and p in {5,7,11} passed. The smallest permitted instance was also proved directly. The extension b(0)=1 is harmless: both arguments of b in the conjecture are positive. The source still labels the supercongruence a conjecture, while the linked 2016 paper establishes integrality. OEIS's main pages were access-blocked, so its official data mirror was used. The cited 1974 JSTOR article was also access-blocked; Gould's posed claim was verified through OEIS, and integrality through the accessible primary paper. Experiments are confined to /workspace/review/.
